item.description:
**Download:** [Leise-2.2.5.zip](https://github.com/ramonfeng/leise/releases/download/v2.2.5/Leise-2.2.5.zip) — quit Leise, then replace the old `Leise.app` in your Applications folder. (First launch after replacing: System Settings → Privacy & Security → "Open Anyway", same as before — [README](https://github.com/ramonfeng/leise#readme).)
## What changed in 2.2.5
- **German spoken numbers become digits — in every shape they come out of your mouth.** "vier Punkt dreiundneunzig" → 4.93, "zwei Komma" → "2,", version chains → 2.2.5, fused tokens ("zweiPunkt"), English "point", and German numbers spoken inside Chinese sentences (even glued to the characters) all land as Arabic numerals now — mid-sentence, at sentence start, and inside chains like 2.2.6. - **German words stop being starved out of recognition.** The recognition-bias budget now orders your dictionary by how often each word actually lands in your dictations, reserves guaranteed room for the built-in German administrative vocabulary and for whatever is on your screen, and counts multi-word entries ("NEORUBY GmbH") correctly — the words you rely on stop being the first ones cut. - **The cursor-jump / text-vanish in Claude Code Desktop is fixed at the root.** That app periodically restores an older draft of its input box, wiping freshly dictated sentences; Leise now recognizes the rollback signature and re-delivers the missing text in one coherent paste instead of leaving fragments behind a jumped cursor. - **The same word spoken once no longer lands twice in different scripts.** Repeated terms where one rendering came out Latin and the other in Chinese characters (a brand name, a street, an invoice word) are now recognized as the same audio and deduplicated. - **The polish-skip notification tells you what actually happened.** When the polish model would have translated your words instead of polishing them, it is skipped — and the notification now says your dictation was delivered as spoken, nothing lost.
## The essentials (unchanged)
**Apple Silicon only** (M1 or newer) · **macOS 14.4+** · about **7 GB free disk** (523 MB app + 5.9 GB speech models downloaded on first run).
A 100 % local dictation app for macOS. Your audio and your transcripts never leave your Mac; it works with the network off.
